newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia summons Sidanko, KomiTEK over taxes.
newsitem.headline: Russia summons Sidanko, KomiTEK over taxes.

text.p: Russia's Federal Bankruptcy Administration (FUDN) said on Wednesday it had summoned the officials from oil groups NK Sidanko and KomiTEK to discuss their subsidiaries' tax arrears and debts to the pension fund.
A bankruptcy administration statement said Sidanko subsidiaries owed 1.52 trillion roubles ($275.2 million), and KomiTEK subsidiaries owed 290 billion roubles.
The statement said officials from 14 other companies had also been summoned to discuss tax problems.
It said Sidanko subsidiary Kondpetroleum owed 564.2 billion roubles in tax arrears and 227 billion roubles in pension contributions.
Sidanko is one of a dozen vertically integrated Russian oil groups created over the last few years.
Apart from Kondpetroleum, its main operating units are Chernogorneft and Varyoganneftegaz, which were not named in the statement.
But the administration said Tebukneft, a subsidiary of regional oil company KomiTEK's main operating unit Komineft owed 122.3 billion roubles in tax arrears.
The authorities have recently threatened to declare a number of prominent companies bankrupt if they do not pay their taxes.
Russia is under pressure from the International Monetary Fund to improve tax collection in order to qualify for regular payments under a $10 billion loan programme.
Tax revenues are running at only about 75 percent of budgeted levels this year, forcing the government to slash spending to prevent the budget deficit from ballooning.
